📌 Reentrancy: How a Smart Contract Can Open the Door to an Attack

Main Points
⏺ Reentrancy happens when a contract gives control to an external contract too early
⏺ An attacker can call the function again before balances are updated
⏺ This post explains why execution order can decide the safety of funds

1️⃣ Core Idea — a contract sends funds or calls another contract, and that contract jumps back into the original function.
2️⃣ The Problem — if the user balance is reduced after sending funds, the attacker may withdraw multiple times.
3️⃣ Why It’s Dangerous — the contract “thinks” funds are still available even though withdrawal already started.
4️⃣ Common Defense — update state first, send funds after, and use protective locks.
5️⃣ Practical Check — if a protocol handles withdrawals, external calls, and complex logic, audits matter a lot.

Final Thoughts

Reentrancy is an attack on execution order. Sometimes the bug is not what the contract does, but when it does it.

Ireland Plays, Then Boycotts the Ritual

Ireland will play Israel on Sunday in Debrecen, Hungary. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu will not. The squad voted by a “significant majority” to fulfill the fixture, then decided that handshakes, pennants and ordinary pre-match politeness were apparently too much football.

Bazunu withdrew from the squad, saying participation would be wrong because of his personal conviction that “the killing of innocent people is wrong.” He was the only player to leave the team. Reports that seven other players had also refused to play were not borne out by the Football Association of Ireland’s statement or by manager Heimir Hallgrímsson, who said the rest of the squad trained. 

The Ireland players will wear black armbands “in recognition of all lives lost in the conflict.” They will not take part in some elements of the pre-match ceremony, will not exchange pennants or shake hands with Israeli players, and will suspend media duties for the rest of the international window. The FAI and players also plan to donate match fees and proceeds from Ireland’s October 1 match against Austria to charity. 

A collective boycott would have forfeited the match and exposed the association to UEFA sanctions. The players chose a narrower version: play the 90 minutes, reject the ceremony and turn the warm-up into a political statement. UEFA gets its fixture. Ireland gets its protest. Bazunu gets the only act that costs a place on the team. 

Israeli midfielder Dor Peretz said Israel would offer handshakes regardless. Coach Ran Ben Shimon said he planned to shake Hallgrímsson’s hand and did not want to “make a big story” out of it. That leaves the Irish squad preparing a gesture meant to deny normality while the Israelis prepare to act normally.

Ireland is not boycotting Israel. It is boycotting the part of football where opponents pretend the match is only football.

🌐 Bitcoin price targets $72.5K as Aroon favors sellers 

🔖 Bitcoin price fell toward $75,500 after the U.S. Senate rejected the CLARITY Act, while bearish momentum and nearby liquidation clusters raised the risk of another decline before the Federal Reserve’s rate decision. Bitcoin price fell toward $75,500 after the U.S. Senate rejected the CLARITY Act, while bearish momentum and nearby liquidation clusters raised the risk of another decline before the Federal Reserve’s rate decision.

❗️ The procedural vote ended 49-50, leaving the proposed crypto market structure legislation 11 votes short of the 60 required to move forward. The setback weighed on digital assets and U.S.-listed crypto companies as traders reassessed the outlook for federal market rules. Derivatives amplified the initial decline. Approximately $771 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including about $568 million in long positions, according to market data cited after the vote. The imbalance showed that traders positioned for higher prices were caught by Bitcoin’s move below $76,000.

🔗 BTC also briefly fell through the lower Bollinger Band, which stood near $75,244, before returning inside the indicator. A move outside the lower band can signal heavy selling, but re-entry alone does not confirm that the correction has ended. The 4-hour relative strength index stood at 37.23, below its signal average of 45.70. RSI remains above the conventional oversold boundary of 30, leaving room for further weakness if buyers fail to defend the $75,000 region.
